result.note: Tests the August 2026 PM-KISAN extension outlay and the scheme's beneficiary group.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, India extended the PM-KISAN scheme. Consider the following statements:
items: The scheme provides income support to landless agricultural labourers rather than landholding farmers.
The extension, covering five more years, carries an outlay of INR 3.16 trillion.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because PM-KISAN supports eligible landholding farmer families, not landless labourers. The five-year extension costs INR 3.16 trillion (USD 33.1 billion), but the per-family payout has not changed since 2019 and is shrinking in real terms.
questions.source: India locked in five more years of PM-KISAN farmer payments at INR 3.16 trillion (USD 33.1 billion), with the per-family payout unchanged since 2019 and shrinking in real terms.
